predictive_services_discussion: 8/5/2026 Breezy west winds 12-20 mph with gusts 20-30 mph amid relative humidity 4-10% will develop along the Sierra Front and from the central Great Basin to the West Slope and southwest Wyoming. Temperatures will continue to be hot in the southern half of the West, with above normal temperatures in the northern half of the West, as well, as temperatures near 100°F expected in the Willamette Valley. Very low relative humidity 4-15% is also expected in much of California to the Inland Northwest and northern Rockies, and overnight recovery will be poor and less than 30% for most mid-slopes and ridges. Locally gusty east winds up to 30 mph are expected in the Columbia Gorge in the morning before weakening in the afternoon. The southern Plains will also experience extreme heat near 105°F, with locally breezy south winds and low relative humidity. Scattered showers and thunderstorms will develop in southeast Arizona, with isolated dry thunderstorms possible in northern New Mexico to extreme southern Colorado. Scattered showers and thunderstorms are also expected in Florida, bringing some short-term relief to the ongoing drought. Showers and thunderstorms will develop from the central Plains to the Great Lakes along a cold front, with isolated showers and thunderstorms from the Appalachians to the East Coast. Above normal temperatures will continue across eastern Alaska today, with dry conditions expected to persist through the weekend.
